nodes.description: Mutant Nav1.5 channels perturb voltage-sensing gating and sodium current in cardiomyocytes: in humanized D1275N knock-in mice, Nav1.5 protein abundance, peak depolarizing sodium current, and cardiac conduction velocity are reduced in a gene-dose-dependent manner in both heterozygous (DN/H) and homozygous (DN/DN) animals, whereas increased persistent late sodium current and spontaneous arrhythmias were observed only in homozygous (DN/DN) mice. Clinically in heterozygous human carriers, channel dysfunction manifests as conduction delay, sinus node dysfunction / bradycardia, atrial fibrillation, and ventricular tachycardia in over 90% of mutation carriers, accompanying or preceding ventricular dilation.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion in CMD1E is a heterozygous variant in SCN5A, encoding the alpha subunit of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.5. The founding allele is Asp1275Asn (D1275N), identified after refined locus mapping in a family with dilated cardiomyopathy and rhythm disturbance, and two-thirds of reported DCM-associated SCN5A missense variants cluster in the highly conserved S3 and S4 voltage-sensing transmembrane segments (e.g., R222Q). Unlike sarcomeric or cytoskeletal DCM genes, Nav1.5 is an ion channel whose other alleles cause the primary channelopathies Brugada syndrome, LQT3, and progressive cardiac conduction disease.

nodes.description: Carriers develop the defining structural remodeling of dilated cardiomyopathy - left ventricular chamber enlargement with impaired systolic function - with characteristically early onset. Myocardial interstitial fibrosis is heterogeneous across CMD1E alleles and disease stages: human endomyocardial biopsies from SCN5A T220I and R814W carriers show myocyte hypertrophy with mild-to-marked interstitial fibrosis and aged heterozygous Scn5a-deficient mice develop myocardial fibrosis, whereas D1275N and 2550-2551insTG human biopsies and 12-week-old humanized D1275N knock-in mice (which show gene-dose-dependent left ventricular dilatation and fractional-shortening reduction across DN/H heterozygotes and DN/DN homozygotes) lack significant histological fibrosis, indicating that ionic and electromechanical dysfunction can initiate chamber dilation before or without extensive fibrotic replacement.
